subject: kinkajou
title: This Animal Turns Its Feet Backwards to Run Down Trees Headfirst

scenes.text: This animal turns its feet around backwards, and runs down trees headfirst.
It looks like a monkey, but the kinkajou is related to raccoons.
It can rotate its hind feet 180 degrees, so its claws grip the bark on the way down.
Its tail grabs branches like a fifth hand. Only one other carnivore has a tail like that.
And its five-inch tongue reaches deep into flowers for nectar, dusting its face with pollen.
So a raccoon relative ended up as a rainforest pollinator, upside down.

description:
The kinkajou is a raccoon relative from Central and South American rainforests that behaves more like a monkey.
It can rotate its hind feet 180 degrees to climb down headfirst, has a prehensile tail shared only with the binturong among carnivores, and uses a five-inch tongue to drink nectar, helping pollinate flowers.
Did you think it was a monkey?
first_comment: The other carnivore with a grabbing tail is the binturong, which smells like popcorn. Which would you rather meet at night?
